analyst_view.overall: Early view: Académico Viseu are 6th after a run of six straight wins that ended with a 1-0 defeat at Nacional in the rescheduled, fog-delayed game, followed by an extra stay in Madeira when flights were cancelled. Alverca are 11th under Sérgio Ferreira, lead the league in tackles, and lose Yaya Bojang, Dawda Camara and Samy Merheg to national teams during the break. Bruno Pinheiro admitted his team were 'uninspired' going forward last time.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean a little lower: Pinheiro said Académico were short of ideas in attack at Nacional, Alverca striker Dawda Camara has not scored for over a month, and Nabil Touaizi has had a calf relapse. Alverca's tackling game tends to break play up rather than open it.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners, with Alverca oddly expected to win more than the hosts. Académico won six in a row mostly through efficiency rather than territory, so the split is plausible. Nothing I found moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean higher: Alverca make more tackles than anyone in the league, and their recent games have included a red card for Baseya after six minutes against Arouca. Académico's home win over Rio Ave ended in a brawl that cost their team manager a 30-day ban, so tempers have run hot at the Fontelo.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, which is high for two mid-table sides. Alverca's pressing and tackling game produces a stop-start match, and Académico's last outing was short on attacking ideas. I expect a figure in the low twenties.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. With Camara out of form and Touaizi doubtful for Alverca, and Académico's attack stalling at Nacional, I lean lower. Around 8 looks more realistic.
